summary: Deep audit of cchsflow R/recode-with-table.R (983 lines). Structure: rec_with_table (entry, lines 154-245: loads worksheets via data(), deparse(substitute()) database naming, list-vs-data.frame branch) -> recode_call (248-351: variable filtering by character vector or variables-sheet merge, var_labels patching, grepl database row filter) -> recode_columns (431-691: 3-way row split into map::/DerivedVar::/plain, per-variable while loop with else handling, bracket-interval parsing, compare_value_based_on_interval, log_table, notes; then derived-variable while loop) -> recode_derived_variables (827-973: recursive feeder resolution with var_stack cycle detection, rowwise()+do() per-row dispatch) -> calculate_custom_function_row_value (974-983: unname + do.call positional dispatch). Labeling delegated to R/label-utils.R (create_label_list_element, label_data); column-name constants in R/strings.R pkg.globals (which carries a large dead inventory of bllflow-era constants: bllFlowContent.*, tableOne.*, LongTable.*, WorkingData.*, FunctionList.* used nowhere outside strings.R). Two high-severity bugs were PROVEN LIVE against the loaded package: (1) list-mode rec_with_table recodes every database with the FIRST database's rules (the loop passes the whole database_name vector to recode_call; grepl uses only pattern[1] with warnings); (2) the interval parser silently mangles set-syntax recStart like '[7,8,9]' into the interval [7,8], dropping 9 to the else row -- 14 production worksheet rows (HUI_01..HUI_09) use this syntax and are only coincidentally correct because their else row maps to the same NA::b. Also proven live: a plain data.frame is routed into the list branch whenever ncol(data) == length(database_name) because is.list() is TRUE for data.frames; and the categorical/continuous missing-data split where categoricals receive literal string sentinels 'NA(b)' while continuous receive haven::tagged_na, with as.factor()/factor() coercion (engine line 953, label-utils line 186) destroying tagged NAs returned by v3 derived functions. The derived-variable dispatch uses deprecated dplyr rowwise()+do() (superseded since dplyr 1.0.0, 2020) with bare-character-vector select() (tidyselect >=1.1 deprecation) and calls each custom function once per data row via unnamed positional do.call, so argument order silently couples worksheet variableStart order to function formals. The roxygen documentation promises sjmisc::rec features (comma lists, colon ranges, min/max/lo/hi, NA-as-recFrom) that the engine does not implement and the worksheet does not use, and documents wrong defaults for append_to_data and notes. log= prints a per-variable recode table and notes= prints worksheet notes, but both are silently ignored for DerivedVar:: variables. custom_function_path is source()d into the global environment despite a comment claiming a new environment, and get() resolution lets worksheet Func:: cells invoke any reachable global function. Dead code: map:: row split never consumed, append_non_db_columns hardcoded FALSE, '(,)' interval branch unreachable, factor-levels append no-op from the stringsAsFactors era, is_equal(x,'character(0)') literal-string comparison, '. <- NULL' NSE hack, pointless assign() side effect. Issue count: 4 high, 9 medium, 8 low.

issues.title: List-mode recoding applies the first database's rules to every database (silent data corruption)
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:188-203 -- for (data_name in database_name) loop passes database_name = database_name (the FULL vector), not data_name, to recode_call
/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:320 -- grepl(database_name, variable_details$databaseStart) uses only pattern[1] when given a vector

Live repro (Rscript, devtools::load_all): list(db_one, db_two) with distinct rules (db_two recodes to 991/992) returned db_two$TEST_VAR == c('1','2') -- db_one's rules -- plus six 'argument pattern has length > 1 and only the first element will be used' warnings
/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/tests/testthat/test-recode-with-table.R (39 lines) -- zero list-mode tests; only 4 single-data.frame golden tests
issues.why_design_issue: A documented API mode ('data ... Can also be a list of dataframes', doc lines 103-107) silently produces wrong harmonized data for every database after the first. This is exactly the class of silent cross-cycle error the package exists to prevent, and it is invisible unless the user notices grepl warnings.
issues.candidate_fix: Pass data_name (the loop variable) to recode_call; also apply attach_data_name in this branch; add list-mode regression test with per-database rules. One-line fix plus tests in v3; in v4, make database identity an explicit per-call argument rather than a regex filter.

issues.title: Interval parser silently mangles set-syntax recStart ('[7,8,9]' becomes interval [7,8], third value dropped to else)
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:571-601 -- strsplit on ',' but only from_values[[1]] and [[2]] are used; third element ignored; interval_right becomes '8' -> invalid -> silently replaced by default '[,]' (lines 604-609)

Live repro: recStart '[7,8,9]' -> recEnd NA::b with else -> 2 produced SRC 7,8 -> 'NA(b)' but SRC 9 -> '2' (else), with runtime message 'invalid interval was passed. Default interval will be used: [,]'
Worksheet scan (Rscript read.csv on inst/extdata/variable_details.csv): 14 rows use recStart '[7,8,9]' across HUI_01..HUI_09; only coincidentally correct because their else row is also NA::b

/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:571-574 -- bracket detection regex '\\[*\\]' / '\\(*\\)' actually matches ANY string containing ']' or ')' (the * quantifies the bracket, not a wildcard), so any stray bracket in recStart enters the interval path and a one-element split crashes at from_values[[2]]
issues.why_design_issue: The engine accepts-and-mangles worksheet syntax that authors evidently believed valid, with no validation layer; correctness currently depends on a coincidence in the else rows. A grammar the parser does not reject is a grammar it must implement.
issues.candidate_fix: Define and validate a formal recStart grammar (single value | [a,b] with (/[ variants | else | else copy); error loudly on >2 comma elements or unparseable cells; fix the bracket-detection regex to '^\\[.*\\]$' style anchors. In v4 move validation into check-worksheets so bad syntax never reaches the engine.

issues.title: Split missing-data regime: literal 'NA(b)' string sentinels for categoricals vs haven::tagged_na for continuous; factor coercion destroys tagged NAs
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:807-825 -- recode_variable_NA_formating: cat -> paste('NA(', tag, ')') string; cont -> haven::tagged_na(tag)
Live repro output: categorical TEST_VAR values are the literal string/factor level 'NA(b)', not NA

/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:949-954 -- derived cat variables coerced with as.factor(unlist(...)); live demo: as.factor(c(1,2,tagged_na('b'))) loses the 'b' tag (na_tag NA after round trip)
/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/label-utils.R:184-186 -- label_data re-factors any non-factor cat column, same tag destruction
/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/bmi.R:203 -- v3 functions (e.g. calculate_bmi pathway) return haven::tagged_na('b'), so v3 3-step outputs routed through the cat branch lose missing-reason detail
issues.why_design_issue: Two incompatible missingness encodings live in one output dataframe: is.na() is FALSE for categorical missing ('NA(b)' is a level), TRUE for continuous missing, and the tag detail v3 functions carefully produce is destroyed at the engine boundary for cat-typed deriveds. This directly blocks the v4 goal of a coherent metadata-driven missing-data contract and contaminates downstream tables/models.
issues.candidate_fix: Pick one representation per output contract (haven labelled + tagged_na, or explicit factor missing levels) and apply it uniformly in one boundary function; never coerce through as.factor/as.character for values carrying tags. This is an architecture decision for the v4 engine, with a migration shim for v3.

issues.title: Derived-variable dispatch: deprecated rowwise()+do() calling custom functions once per row via unnamed positional do.call
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:937-947 -- recoded_data %>% rowwise() %>% select(used_feeder_vars) %>% do(column_being_added = calculate_custom_function_row_value(., ...)); do() superseded since dplyr 1.0.0 (2020); select() with a bare character vector triggers the tidyselect >=1.1 'use all_of()' deprecation

/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:974-983 -- row_values <- unname(row_values); do.call(get(custom_function_name), row_values): arguments matched purely by POSITION, so worksheet variableStart order must match the function's formals order; a transposition is silent wrong data
/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:150 -- @importFrom dplyr rowwise select do case_when (engine itself never uses case_when)
Per-row dispatch means an n-row CCHS cycle (~100k rows) incurs n R function calls per derived variable even though every v3 function is vectorized (CEP-017 context)
issues.why_design_issue: The dispatch relies on two deprecated dplyr idioms slated for eventual removal, has O(rows) interpretive overhead that dominates rec_with_table runtime for derived variables, and the unnamed positional contract is the single most dangerous coupling in the package: nothing checks that feeder order matches formals.
issues.candidate_fix: Replace with a single vectorized call: do.call(fun, setNames(as.list(recoded_data[used_feeder_vars]), names(formals(fun))[seq_along(used_feeder_vars)])) after asserting length/name compatibility against formals(); fall back to mapply only for genuinely scalar functions. v4 should require named argument binding declared in the worksheet or function metadata.

issues.title: Plain data.frame routed into the list branch when ncol(data) == length(database_name)
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:186-187 -- if (is.list(data) && length(database_name) == length(data)): is.list() is TRUE for every data.frame and length(df) is its column count
Live repro: a 1-column data.frame with one database_name errored 'The data testdb is missing from the passed list please verify the names are correct'
issues.why_design_issue: Type dispatch by duck-typing on is.list() misclassifies the most common input type; the failure mode is an unrelated error message that points users at a 'list' they never passed.
issues.candidate_fix: Test is.data.frame(data) first, and treat the list branch as 'is.list(data) && !is.data.frame(data)'; validate names(data) against database_name explicitly.

issues.title: Roxygen documents sjmisc::rec features the engine does not implement (comma lists, colon ranges, min/max/lo/hi, NA as recFrom)
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:75-100 -- docs promise recFrom '1,2', '1:4', 'min:4', lo/hi tokens, and recFrom 'NA'

/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:571-616 -- parser only handles bracket intervals, single values, else, copy; a comma list without brackets goes to the scalar branch and as.numeric('1,2') -> NA -> string-equality miss
/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:713-717 -- recFrom 'NA' can never match data NAs: which('NA' == col) drops NA comparisons, so the documented NA-recode feature is impossible
Worksheet scan: 0 colon ranges, 0 comma lists without brackets, 0 min/max/lo/hi tokens, 0 bare-NA recStart in 3,839 rows -- the features are unused as well as unimplemented
Doc default mismatches: lines 113-114 claim append_to_data default TRUE (code line 160: FALSE); lines 117-118 claim notes default FALSE (code line 162: TRUE)
issues.why_design_issue: The user-facing contract is inherited verbatim from bllflow/sjmisc and is fiction; worksheet authors reading the help page will write rows the engine silently never matches. Wrong documented defaults additionally invert the user's mental model of what the function returns and prints.
issues.candidate_fix: Rewrite the roxygen to describe the actual grammar and defaults now (S); in v4, generate documentation from the validated grammar definition so docs and parser cannot drift.

issues.title: log= and notes= are silently ignored for derived (DerivedVar::) variables
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:827-973 -- log and print_note are parameters of recode_derived_variables but are only ever passed through the recursive call (lines 916-917); no message/print uses them
/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:634-643 and 646-659 -- note printing and the log_table print exist only in the plain-recode path

/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:545-548,619-623 -- log_table is built row-by-row even when log = FALSE (wasted work); line 606-609 'invalid interval' message prints unconditionally regardless of log/notes
issues.why_design_issue: The two observability switches the API offers cover only half the engine; derived variables -- the riskiest transformations -- produce no recode log and never surface their worksheet notes. Meanwhile unconditional message() calls (also lines 171-183 on default loading) cannot be turned off except via suppressMessages.
issues.candidate_fix: v4: a structured logging object (per-variable provenance: rows matched per rule, feeder functions called, notes) returned or emitted through one verbosity control; v3 stopgap: print feeder/function info under log and notes in the derived path, and gate the interval message behind a warning.

issues.title: custom_function_path is source()d into the global environment despite comment claiming a new environment; get() dispatch resolves any reachable function
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:166-169 -- comment 'If custom Functions are passed create new environment and source' followed by bare source(custom_function_path); source() default local=FALSE evaluates in globalenv, polluting/overwriting user bindings

/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:980 -- do.call(get(custom_function_name), ...): get() walks function env -> namespace -> imports -> base -> globalenv, so any Func:: cell in a worksheet executes whatever function of that name is reachable, with no allowlist
issues.why_design_issue: Comment-code mismatch hides a real side effect (global namespace pollution and silent overwriting of user functions), and worksheet data effectively names arbitrary code to execute -- a robustness and provenance problem for a package whose worksheets are community-edited CSVs.
issues.candidate_fix: source(custom_function_path, local = fn_env <- new.env(parent = asNamespace('cchsflow'))) and resolve via get(name, envir = fn_env, inherits = TRUE) with an explicit registry/allowlist of derivation functions; error with a clear message when the function is not found.

issues.title: Error path in get_data_variable_name references undefined 'row', masking the real error with a closure-coercion failure
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:394-410 -- stop(paste('The row', row, 'for the variable', ...)): no 'row' exists in this function's scope; it resolves to base::row (a function)

Live check: paste('x', row, 'y') errors 'cannot coerce type closure to vector of type character', so users hitting a databaseStart/variableStart mismatch see an inscrutable coercion error instead of the diagnostic message
issues.why_design_issue: The one diagnostic that explains a common worksheet authoring mistake (database missing from variableStart) is unreachable; debugging cost lands on every worksheet contributor.
issues.candidate_fix: Drop 'row' from the message or pass the row index/variable row in as an argument; add a unit test that asserts the error message text.

issues.title: Database matching is unanchored regex substring matching (grepl without fixed=TRUE or tokenization)
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:320 -- grepl(database_name, variable_details$databaseStart): database_name used as a regex pattern against comma-separated cell text; 'cchs2015' would match 'cchs2015_2016_p' rows

/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:378,382 -- grepl(data_name, var_start_names) inside variableStart parsing, same substring semantics; a database name occurring inside a variable name is a false positive
No escaping of regex metacharacters anywhere in the path
issues.why_design_issue: Era/cycle identifiers differ by suffixes ('cchs2009_s' vs 'cchs2009_2010_s' family); substring semantics make near-miss database names silently select the wrong rule rows instead of erroring, the exact failure class the team already tracks for worksheet QA.
issues.candidate_fix: strsplit(databaseStart, ',') + trimws + exact %in% matching; same tokenization for variableStart 'db::var' pairs; validate the requested database_name against the known database list and error on no exact match.

issues.title: recode_variable_NA_formating is fragile: substring 'NA' trigger and unguarded [[3]] crash on malformed cells
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:809 -- grepl('NA', cell_value): any recEnd merely containing the letters 'NA' enters the tagged-NA path

/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:810-814 -- strsplit(cell_value, ':')[[1]] then na_value_list[[3]]: a bare 'NA' cell (or 'NA:a') errors 'subscript out of bounds' with no context; worksheet currently has 1,495 'NA::' rows and 0 bare-NA rows so the crash is latent, awaiting one typo
No validation that the tag is a single letter a-z as haven::tagged_na requires
issues.why_design_issue: The central missingness parser trusts its input completely; one malformed worksheet cell produces an uncontextualized crash deep in the engine instead of a row-addressed validation error.
issues.candidate_fix: Anchor with regexpr '^NA::([a-z])$'; on mismatch raise an error naming the variable and cell content; share the same parse with the worksheet checker so it is caught at authoring time.

issues.title: No dependency resolution against the full worksheet: feeder variables must be explicitly listed in `variables`
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:270-286 -- variable_details is subset to the requested variables BEFORE recoding; the recursive feeder search (lines 908-928) only sees this filtered set

/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:866-890 -- requesting only 'HWTGBMI_der' without 'HWTGHTM','HWTGWTK' triggers the 'could not be derived because ... was never specified' warning and the variable is silently absent from output

/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:871-877 -- the warning interpolates feeder_vars (all unresolved feeders) rather than non_func_missing_variables (the actual missing set), so the message can blame the wrong variables
Examples (doc lines 127-141) work around this by always listing feeders alongside the derived variable
issues.why_design_issue: The engine contains a recursion and cycle detector that could resolve dependencies, but upfront filtering cripples it; users must hand-maintain transitive feeder lists, and failure is a warning plus a missing column rather than either auto-resolution or a hard error. CEP-015 variable-tools exists partly to paper over this.
issues.candidate_fix: Resolve the feeder closure against the FULL variable_details before filtering (keep requested variables as the output set, feeders as intermediate, dropped unless append requested); fix the warning to report non_func_missing_variables; v4: explicit dependency graph as a first-class object.

issues.title: Row-indexing mismatch between variable_rows and fun_variable_rows in derived processing; early return abandons remaining Func rows
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:853-861 -- loop runs seq_len(nrow(fun_variable_rows)) but feeder_vars are read from variable_rows[row_num, ] (ALL rows for the variable, including category-label rows), while the function name is read from fun_variable_rows[row_num, ] (line 931-933): positional indices into two differently filtered frames
/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:879-890 -- on missing feeders the function returns from INSIDE the for loop, skipping any remaining Func rows for that variable
/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:955-956 -- multiple Func rows for one variable each overwrite the whole column; last writer wins with no warning
issues.why_design_issue: Works today only because every row of a derived variable shares one variableStart cell; any worksheet where label rows precede the Func row with a different variableStart (e.g. era-specific deriveds) reads feeders from the wrong row -- a correctness landmine for exactly the multi-era harmonization v3 is adding.
issues.candidate_fix: Iterate over fun_variable_rows only and take feeders from the same row object; warn or error if a variable has multiple Func rows matching one database; continue (not return) on unresolvable rows.

issues.title: Dead code inventory: map:: split never consumed, append_non_db_columns hardcoded, unreachable '(,)' branch, no-op levels() append, 'character(0)' literal comparison, '. <- NULL' hack, pointless assign()
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:439-441 -- map_variables_to_process computed and never referenced again; 0 'map::' rows exist in inst/extdata/variable_details.csv, and any such row would be silently dropped (rec filter at 448-451 excludes them)
/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:185 -- append_non_db_columns <- FALSE hardcoded, making lines 332-342 unreachable while the flag is plumbed through two function signatures

/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:741-748 -- '(,)' interval branch unreachable from the engine: valid_intervals (line 455) excludes it and lines 604-609 coerce anything invalid to '[,]' first

/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:549-551 -- levels(recoded_data[[var]]) <- c(levels(...), levels(character_column)) is a stringsAsFactors-era no-op (levels() of a character column is NULL)

/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:516-517 -- !is_equal(else_value, 'character(0)') compares against the literal STRING 'character(0)'; the intended zero-length check is already covered by length(else_value)==1, so the clause is dead
/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:1-2 -- '. <- NULL' R CMD check hack for the do() pronoun, with cryptic comment '# Removing Note'

/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:962-963 -- label_list[[var]] <- assign(var, create_label_list_element(...)): assign() is used purely for its return value, creating a stray local binding named after the CCHS variable (would shadow locals like 'label_list' if a variable carried such a name)

/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/strings.R:43-101 -- bllFlowContent.*, tableOne.*, LongTable.*, Modules.*, WorkingData.*, FunctionList.* constants referenced nowhere else in R/ (grep confirms only strings.R)
issues.why_design_issue: Roughly a fifth of the engine is vestigial bllflow scaffolding; every dead path raises the comprehension cost of an already 983-line file and misleads contributors about what worksheet syntax (map::) is supported.
issues.candidate_fix: Delete dead branches and constants in a mechanical cleanup commit gated by the existing golden tests; replace the '.' hack with utils::globalVariables or eliminate it when do() goes.

issues.title: compare_value_based_on_interval uses an obfuscated x %in% x[which(cond)] construction instead of direct vectorized comparison
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:712-755 -- every branch computes data[[col]] %in% data[[col]][which(cond)]: builds the satisfying VALUE set then re-tests membership, i.e. a double pass + hash to express coalesce(cond, FALSE)
Side effect relied upon implicitly: %in% maps NA comparisons to FALSE, which is the only reason NAs in source data fall through to the else row
issues.why_design_issue: The core matching primitive hides its NA semantics inside an idiom no reviewer reads correctly on first pass; the NA-to-FALSE behaviour that the whole else/NA::b system depends on is an accident of %in%, not a stated contract.
issues.candidate_fix: Rewrite as cond <- (lo <= x & x <= hi) (per interval); return cond & !is.na(cond), with a comment stating that NA never matches a rule and falls to else. Behaviour-preserving, testable.

issues.title: Quadratic/per-cell recode loop: per-variable while-loop with repeated dataframe filtering and per-category column assignment
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:459-468 -- while (nrow(rec_variables_to_process) > 0) re-filters the rows dataframe twice per variable

/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:632-633 -- recoded_data[valid_row_index, variable] <- value executes one full-length logical-index data.frame assignment per worksheet category row (3,839 rows in the current worksheet), each triggering data.frame copy semantics
/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:491-507 -- O(n^2) duplicate-From detection loop (sum over the vector inside a for over the vector)
/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:545-548,619-623 -- log_table assembled cell-by-cell even when log = FALSE
issues.why_design_issue: Combined with per-row derived dispatch this makes rec_with_table the slowest step of every cchsflow pipeline; for v4's goal of running all variables across all cycles, an O(categories x rows) data.frame-assignment engine does not scale.
issues.candidate_fix: v4: compile each variable's rules to a lookup/join (data.frame of from-interval -> to) applied via findInterval/match once per variable on plain vectors; use duplicated() for the dup check; build the log from rule-match counts already computed.

issues.title: attach_data_name only honoured in the single-data.frame branch
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:229-231 -- data[['data_name']] <- database_name applied only in the data.frame branch; the list branch (188-214) never applies it despite the parameter being documented generically (line 121-122)
issues.why_design_issue: Provenance tagging is precisely most useful when recoding multiple cycles for bind_rows, the one mode where it silently does nothing.
issues.candidate_fix: Set data[[data_name]][['data_name']] <- data_name inside the list-branch loop; add to the list-mode regression test.

issues.title: Variables-sheet path silently drops unknown variables and reorders rows via merge(); character-vector path warns
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:788-792 -- rows for variables absent from the variables sheet are filtered out with no message, whereas the character-vector path (277-285) warns about requested-but-missing variables

/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:780-787 -- merge() with default sort=TRUE reorders variable_details rows, changing label 'first row' selection and processing order between the two input modes
issues.why_design_issue: Two input modes for the same parameter have different silence/ordering semantics; users switching from a name vector to a worksheet subset lose the missing-variable diagnostics without notice.
issues.candidate_fix: merge(..., sort = FALSE); emit the same missing-variable warning in both paths; long term collapse the dual-typed `variables` parameter into two explicit arguments.

issues.title: API surface and hygiene: dual-typed `variables` param, exported is_equal, misspelled internals, typo-laden messages, tests relying on partial argument matching
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:104-105 -- `variables` accepts a character vector OR a variables-sheet data.frame (run-time type sniffing at 261-269)
/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/NAMESPACE:110 -- export(is_equal): a generic NA-tolerant comparator exported from a survey-harmonization package's API, also misused internally (line 517)

recode_variable_NA_formating ('formating'), plus message/comment typos: 'instanses' (line 36), 'Detemine' (184), 'varialbe' (470), 'seperate' (383), 'more then once' (500), 'varLalbel' (299), multi-line stop() strings with embedded source indentation (205-213, 232-241)
/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/tests/testthat/test-recode-with-table.R:7 -- tests pass note = FALSE, working only through R partial matching against `notes`
issues.why_design_issue: These are the embarrassment-class defects v4 wants to shed: a flagship function whose own test suite misspells its argument, exported helpers that belong in utils, and user-facing error text with typos and source-code indentation baked in.
issues.candidate_fix: v4: split variables/variables_sheet parameters, soft-deprecate is_equal (lifecycle), rename internals, sweep messages through a single formatter (cli or sprintf), fix tests to use full argument names.

issues.title: Unconditional chatty message() calls not governed by any verbosity control
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:171-182 -- three message() calls fire on every default invocation (no variable_details / no variables / no database_name), with hard-wrapped indentation inside the strings
/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:606-609 -- per-occurrence 'invalid interval' message prints regardless of log/notes settings (observed in live repro)
issues.why_design_issue: The package already exposes log= and notes= but routes none of these through them, so pipelines wrap everything in suppressMessages and thereby also hide genuinely important diagnostics (like the interval mangling).
